Cc: Ravi Mehta <ravi.mehta@lumenbank.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual auth pattern observed (possible credential stuffing)

Hi Evelyn,

We observed a spike in failed token exchange attempts against our integration with Redwood between 2028-07-29T22:45Z and 2028-07-29T23:30Z. A subset of requests succeeded after a short pause — we believe some refresh tokens may have been replayed.

We need:
- A short incident summary from Redwood for our SOC2 record
- Raw request/response logs (redacted PII) and token rotation/timestamp evidence
- Confirmation of any user-facing impact or data exposure

I've included Ravi from our integration team for telemetry correlation. We consider this a moderate-severity finding for our auditors and need artifacts within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Anya Voss
Head of Security, LumenBank
security@lumenbank.com

- No indication of bulk data exfiltration in preliminary scans.
- We'll provide: redwood request logs (token exchange), refresh-token rotation timestamps, and a concise incident summary for your SOC2 package.

Marissa — can you own the SOC2 evidence bundle and liaise on redaction? Karthik — please export the auth logs + token rotation timeline and confirm whether any tokens were rotated invalidated around the window.

Thanks — quick status update: I pulled the auth logs for the window Anya highlighted and ran them through our redaction pipeline.

Deliverables attached to this thread (see attachments):
- lumenbank_auth_logs_20280730.ndjson — request/response traces for 2028-07-29T22:30Z -> 2028-07-29T23:45Z. IPs mapped and redacted per our data-sharing agreement.
- token-rotation-timeline.csv — list of refresh tokens rotated and timestamps.
- sig-caiq-response-lumenbank.pdf — answers to the SIG/CAIQ-specific questions you asked about token handling and retention.

Preliminary findings:
- 82% of failed attempts originated from 3 IP clusters (likely botnets).
- We rotated 14 refresh tokens tied to your tenant at 2028-07-29T23:10:02Z when anomalous reuse was detected. Rotation caused ~0.05% of active sessions to error briefly; that was remediated automatically.
- No additional data access beyond normal API responses was observed.

Next steps we propose:
1) Formal incident summary for your SOC2 auditor (draft attached as PDF).
2) Joint timeline call (30 minutes) to walk through logs and token rotation artifacts — proposed windows tomorrow 09:00 or 16:00 PT.
3) If you'd like, Redwood can add a permanent filtering rule for your tenant IPs to block the offending clusters.

Marissa Cole
Security Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 01 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unusual auth pattern observed (possible credential stuffing) — postmortem and recommendations

Hi all — final summary and attachments below. Apologies for the wall of text but wanted to capture the timeline and mitigations for your auditors.

TL;DR: automated credential stuffing against refresh endpoint; tokens were replayed but short window and rotations prevented unauthorized long-lived access. No customer data exported.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2028-07-29T22:42:11Z — spike in 401s for tenant LumenBank detected by our rate-anomaly detector (rule ANOM-409).
- 2028-07-29T22:45:03Z — first token reuse signature detected (same refresh token presented twice within 4s).
- 2028-07-29T23:10:02Z — automatic bulk rotation initiated for tenant (14 tokens rotated).
- 2028-07-29T23:12:18Z — rotation propagation completed across edge nodes.
- 2028-07-29T23:25:00Z — anomalous traffic subsided to baseline.

Cause: external automated attempts (credential stuffing) against the token refresh endpoint. No evidence of an internal compromise.

Impact:
- Temporary authentication errors for ~0.05% of active sessions during rotation window (handled via retry).
- No access-pattern anomalies indicating data exfiltration.

Remediation and Recommendations:
1) We recommend LumenBank rotate any downstream cached tokens at your edge and confirm reissue policy for long-lived session tokens.
2) Redwood can apply tenant-level IP block/deny lists for the identified clusters (we included IP ranges in the log export).
3) Consider short-term hard rate limit on token refresh calls for your tenant; Redwood can enforce a stricter quota for 72 hours.
4) For SOC2 documentation: see attached redwood-ir-postmortem-20280730.pdf and SIG/CAIQ responses.

Attachments included in this message: redwood-ir-postmortem-20280730.pdf, lumenbank_auth_logs_20280730.ndjson, token-rotation-timeline.csv, sig-caiq-response-lumenbank.pdf

If you'd like a 30-minute walk-through, I can be on a call tomorrow 09:00 PT.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
